newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairie harvest resumes after rain delays.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairie harvest resumes after rain delays.

text.p: Canada's Prairie harvest resumed in the past week after heavy rains delayed swathing and combining, Pioneer Grain Co Ltd said in its crop report for the week ended Sept 11.

British Columbia's Dawson Creek region and Alberta's Peace River Valley swathed 50 to 60 percent of crops before 2.5 to three inches of rain fell on some parts of the region. Some barley in the Peace was harvested.
Alberta's crops were rated 71 percent good and 29 percent fair. About 80 percent of all crops were swathed and 45 percent were harvested. Frost was reported in some areas.
Saskatchewan's northern grainbelt crops were rated 75 percent good and 25 percent fair.
Northwest Saskatchewan swathed 70 percent of cereals, 95 percent of canola with 30 percent of crops combined. Frost in the North Battleford wasn't seen causing serious problems.

North central Saskatchewan swathed 80 percent of crops and combined 25 percent of them. Ergot in wheat and rye will be a degrading factor but the extent was not yet known. Wheat midge was not expected to be a serious problem.
Northeast Saskatchewan swathed 60 percent of crops and combined 10 percent. Saturday's frost caused little damage.

Southwest Saskatchewan's crops were rated nine percent very good, 82 percent good and nine percent fair. A quarter of wheat, durum and flax was swathed while all other crops were 95 percent swathed with most crops 75 percent combined.

Southeast Saskatchewan's crops were rated seven percent very good, 73 percent good and 20 percent fair. Seventy percent of wheat and durum was swathed, 60 percent of oats was swathed, 75 percent of barley, 50 percent of flax, 85 percent of canola was swathed but little combining was completed. Wheat midge damage was not seen as a serious degrading factor.
Eastern Saskatchewan and western Manitoba crops were rated 83 percent good and 17 percent fair with 70 percent swathed and 30 percent combined.

Manitoba saw three to four inches of rain which will adversely affect grades on cereal crops. Ergot and fusarium was still a problem in wheat and barley. Yields were expected to be average. Frost was isolated with damage expected to be minimal. Manitoba needs the rest of September to harvest.
